title: Electrochemistry
description: Fundamentals of electrochemistry including thermodynamics and the electrochemical potential, charge transfer kinetics, and mass transfer. Methods based on controlled potential and controlled current are described; the effects of slow heterogeneous kinetics and the perturbation caused by homogeneous chemistry are discussed.

title: Analytical Spectroscopy
description: Advanced treatment of spectroscopic techniques and instrumentation. Atomic and molecular absorption, emission, and scattering processes and their application to quantitative chemical analysis are outlined. Puts different spectroscopic techniques in perspective and demonstrates most appropriate applications to analytical problems.

title: Optics I - Physical Optics and Electromagnetic Theory
description: Treatment of optical phenomena and interactions between electromagnetic radiation and matter using fundamental electromagnetic laws, with applications to modern spectroscopic methods.

title: Optics II – Light-Matter Interaction and Advanced Spectroscopy
description: Advanced treatment of interactions between electromagnetic radiation and matter, with applications to linear spectroscopy, time-resolved nonlinear methods, high-power light-matter interactions, and optical parametric processes.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 249A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Computational Chemistry
description: Basic concepts, methods, and techniques in computational chemistry: density functional and wavefunction theory, molecular property calculations, analysis tools, potential energy surfaces, vibrational effects, molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Computational Chemistry Laboratory
description: Introduction to the practice of modern computational chemistry through a series of advanced computational experiments.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 250 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Special Topics in Organic Chemistry
description: Advanced topics in organic chemistry.

title: Special Topics in Physical Chemistry
description: Advanced topics in physical chemistry. Materials Fee

title: Special Topics in Computational and Theoretical Chemistry
description: Subjects covered vary from year to year.

title: Special Topics in Quantum Science
description: Advanced topics in quantum science.

title: Materials Chemistry
description: An introduction to crystalline solids, descriptive crystal chemistry, solid-state synthesis and characterization techniques, x-ray and electron diffraction, phase diagrams, electronic band structure of extended solids, semi conductors, and nanoscale inorganic materials.

title: Analytical Methods for Organic Nanomaterials
description: Fundamentals of analytical techniques related to measuring the structure and dynamics of organic nanomaterials. Topics include transmission electron microscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, liquid phase electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, light scattering, small angle X-ray, and neutron scattering.

title: Current Topics in Chemical, Applied, and Materials Physics
description: The subjects covered vary from year to year. Connection between fundamental principles and implementations in practice in science, industry, and technology.

title: Photochemistry
description: Photochemical and photovoltaic processes in molecules and semiconductors; quantum mechanics; statistical thermodynamics; kinetics; and experimental techniques relevant to photon absorption and emission; photochemical charge separation, recombination, and transport of electrons and ions; and interfacial redox chemistry.

title: Technical Communication Skills

title: Independent Study
description: Independent research with Chemistry faculty.

title: Independent Study
description: Directed research on topic determined in consultation with faculty member. A term paper or project is required.

title: Medical Terminology
description: A study of English terms derived from Greek and Latin that are important to contemporary medicine, science, and other professions. Emphasis on development of word-building skills. No prior knowledge of Greek or Latin required.

title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Early Greece
description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from its origins in the Bronze Age to the mid-Archaic period. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, religion, and archaeological remains.

title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Late Archaic and Classical Greece
description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the Late Archaic period to the Classical period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Fourth-Century and Hellenistic Greece
description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the fourth century BCE through to the Hellenistic period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Origins to Roman Republic
description: A survey of the development of Roman civilization from its eighth century BCE beginnings to the civil wars of the first century BCE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Roman Empire
description: A survey of Roman civilization from Augustus’s consolidation of power following the civil wars of the first century BCE to the crisis of the third century CE. Includes social history, literature, art, architecture, and religion.

title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: The Fall of Rome
description: A survey of Roman civilization from the crisis of the third century CE to the so-called “fall of Rome” in 476 CE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

title: Classical Mythology: The Gods
description: An overview of the main myths of the gods of the ancient Greeks and Romans and their influence in contemporary and later literature and art. Includes readings from both ancient and modern sources.

title: Classical Mythology: The Heroes
description: An overview of the main myths of the heroes of the ancient Greeks and Romans and their influence in contemporary and later literature and art. Includes readings from both ancient and modern sources.

title: Classical Mythology: Ancient and Modern Perspectives of Classical Mythology
description: Detailed examination of key Greek and Roman myths, their interpretations, and the influence they have exerted on literature, art, and popular culture in subsequent periods.

title: Special Studies in Classics
description: Lower-division level independent research with Classics faculty.

title: Ancient Persia
description: Survey of the history of Persia in antiquity.

title: Classics and History: The Ancient World
description: Selected topics in society and culture of the Graeco-Roman world. Readings in translation.

title: Classical Mythology
description: Selected myths and legends as used in Classical literature, and their modern interpretations.

title: Topics in Classical Literature in English Translation
description: Studies in selected areas of Classical literature. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Topics in Classical Literature in English Translation
description: Studies in selected areas of Classical literature. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Topics in Classical Reception
description: Studies in selected areas of Classical reception. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Topics in Classical Civilization
description: Studies in selected areas of Classical civilization. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: International Studies and the Classics
description: Develops a broader understanding of the formation of different cultures and countries of Classical times and their impact on the modern world.

title: Senior Capstone

title: Colloquium
description: Students meet faculty members and explore the depth and breadth of a classical education inclusive of and beyond the Greco-Roman antiquity. They are also introduced to ideas and methods of reception of ancient worlds to the present day.

title: Directed Group Study
description: Special topics in Classical studies through directed reading and research.

title: Independent Study in Classics
description: Independent research with Classics faculty.

title: Independent Study
description: Supervised independent research. Subject varies.

title: Research in Classics
description: Research under Classics faculty.

title: Dissertation Research
description: Dissertation research with Classics faculty.

title: Introduction to Psychology
description: Introduction to field of psychology, addressing the application of scientific methods to the study of human development, learning, memory, problem solving, perception, biological mechanisms, emotions and motivation, personality, psychopathology, and effects of diverse social and cultural contexts on human behavior.

title: Psychology Fundamentals
description: Part of a two-course series that provides a comprehensive introduction to psychology. Required for students majoring in Cognitive Sciences or Psychology. Topics include the science of psychology, research methods, biology and behavior, consciousness, sensation, and perception.

title: Psychology Fundamentals
description: Part of a two-course series that provides a comprehensive introduction to psychology. Required for students majoring in Cognitive Sciences or Psychology. Topics include learning and memory, thinking, language and intelligence, human development, emotion, and motivation.

title: Exploratory Data Analysis
description: Learn multiple ways of visualizing data, of transforming data, looking for consistencies and patterns in data, and interpreting these patterns to reach conclusions. Serves as first introduction to computer programming using the R language.

title: Probability and Inference
description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on thorough understanding of the probabilistic and logical basis of formal statistical inference, and the concept of statistical evidence. Applications in R.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 10A with a minimum grade of C-

title: Statistical Models
description: Students learn about standard procedures in statistics for the social sciences, with a focus on linear models for discovering the underlying structure in data. Applications in R.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 10A with a minimum grade of C-

title: MATLAB Programming
description: MATLAB is a mathematical software package for solving quantitative problems often encountered in experimental psychology. Topics include rudiments of programming, statistical analysis of data, matrix algebra, signal processing, graphic visualization, and simulated models of cognitive and perceptual processes.

title: Scientific Python for Research
description: Introduces Python for data analysis and modeling encountered in cognitive science and neuroscience. Topics include data structures, execution control, graphic visualization, and interaction with sound and display interfaces. Application in statistical analysis, model simulation, and stimulus presentation and experimental control.

title: Adolescent Psychology
description: Focuses on psychosocial dynamics of today's adolescents in America emphasizing the quest for identity, independence, values, and sexual orientation. The influence of society, family, school, and peers is analyzed. Strategies for helping troubled adolescents are discussed.

title: Acquisition of Language
description: What children say, what they mean, and what they understand. Theories about the learning of language by one-, two-, and three-year-olds. Comparison of kinds of data on which these theories are based.

title: Neurobiology of Cognition
description: Introduces the neurobiological components of human cognition. Topics include discussion of the cortical structures and functions that underlie these behaviors. Emphasis placed on the development and organization of the healthy brain.

title: Self-Identity and Society
description: Studies sociological contributions to theory and research in social psychology, with focus on the social influences on personality, attitudes, beliefs, and behavior; socialization, human groups, and social interaction.

title: Special Topics in Lower-Division Cognitive Sciences
description: Studies in selected areas of cognitive science at the lower-division level. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences I
description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.

title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences II
description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.
prerequisites_raw: COGS H101A with a minimum grade of C-

title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences III
description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.
prerequisites_raw: COGS H101B with a minimum grade of C-

title: Introduction to Statistical Learning
description: Introduction to statistical learning as a tool for scientific research. Topics include linear regression, logistic regression, model selection, cross-validation, ridge and Lasso regularization, classification trees, ensemble methods, random forests, unsupervised learning, PCA, k-means clustering, Gaussian mixture models, and PLS regression.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 14P or I&C SCI 31 or MATH 9 and (( COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-) or STATS 110 ) and MATH 2B

title: Computational Lab Skills
description: Teaches programming tools, skills, and conventions for collaborative work in computational cognitive science. Topics covered include program structure, version control, random number generation, plotting, basic model fitting, and numerical optimization methods.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 14M or COGS 14P or I&C SCI 31 and (( COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-) or STATS 110 )

title: Cognitive Modeling
description: Cognitive process models analyzed using computational Bayesian methods. Formal statistical specification of models, parameter estimation, model evaluation, and research applications. Covers multinomial process trees, signal detection theory, Thurstone ranking models, item-response theory, decision models, and reaction time models.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 14M or COGS 14P or I&C SCI 31 and (( COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-) or STATS 110 )

title: Neural Analytics
description: Introduces the theoretical foundations and practical applications of neural data analysis. Topics include models of neural signals, neural time series analysis, and machine learning applications in cognitive neuroscience.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 14M or COGS 14P or I&C SCI 31 and (( COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-) or STATS 110 )

title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
description: Read and discuss examples of the primary research leading to the concepts covered in Psychology Fundamentals. Focuses on how this research is conducted and how inferences from it are drawn.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 10A with a minimum grade of C-. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Experimental Psychology
description: Emphasis on design of experiments and analysis of results. Experiments are conducted in laboratory sections.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-

title: Advanced Experimental Psychology
description: Design and analysis of multivalent, factorial, and correlational studies. Students prepare proposals for independent research.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 112A and COGS 112LA . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Research in Experimental Psychology
description: Each student conducts a research project in experimental psychology. The projects are discussed in a seminar format. Written reports on each project are submitted at the end of the quarter.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 112BW and COGS 112LB

title: Research Design
description: An examination of design of studies through the lens of validity of scientific claims. You already know how to perform statistical inference. Here we ask a different, broader question: When is an inference worth believing?
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C- and ( COGS 14P with a minimum grade of C- or I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C-)

title: Learning and Memory
description: Theories in learning and memory research and the methodological tools used to test them. Experimental design, statistical data analysis, and interpretation using hands-on lab exercises and the R programming language.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-

title: Experimental Psychology Laboratory
description: Required laboratory section and co-requisite for COGS 112A .

title: Advanced Experimental Psychology Laboratory
description: Required laboratory section for COGS 112BW .

title: Research in Experimental Psychology
description: Required laboratory section and co-requisite for COGS 112C .

title: Learning and Memory Lab
description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for COGS 112E .

title: Research Methods in Psychology Laboratory
description: Required laboratory section and co-requisite for COGS 112M .

title: fMRI Research Laboratory
description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for COGS 112N .

title: Research in Perception and Psychophysics Laboratory
description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for COGS 112P .

title: Cognitive Robotics Laboratory
description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for COGS 112R .

title: Research Methods in Psychology
description: Research methods in psychology for majors who wish to fulfill this requirement separately from upper-division writing. Covers both experimental and descriptive research methods, analysis of results, and reading the psychological literature. Research experience is provided in laboratory sections.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-

title: Introduction to fMRI Research
description: Introduction to functional magnetic resonance imaging as a tool in cognitive neuroscience. Covers inferences about brain activity using MRI, evaluates experimental design considerations, and univariate and multivariate statistical analysis approaches.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-

title: Computational Modeling of Behavior
description: Learn how computational models can be used as theoretical tools to predict, evaluate, and interpret psychological data in a number of domains in psychology, such as perception, learning, decision-making, and problem-solving. Focuses on skill development through coding.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C- and ( COGS 14P with a minimum grade of C- or I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C-)

title: Research in Perception and Psychophysics
description: Introduction to design and practice of experiments: students perform auditory, visual, tactile, or other experiments. Emphasis on methodology, finding and reading previous research, generating research ideas, statistical analysis.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-

title: Cognitive Robotics
description: Introduces concepts on experimental design, embodiment, robot construction, and computer programming. Concepts of embodied intelligence and case studies of cognitive robotics are covered in lecture. Simple robots are constructed and programmed to carry out different behavioral experiments in lab.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-

title: Special Topics in Research Methodologies
description: Studies in selected areas of research methodologies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Abnormal Psychology
description: Introduction to psychopathology and behavioral deviations, and the concepts of theories regarding these conditions.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Developmental Psychology
description: A general introduction to the study of the physical, intellectual, social, and emotional development of the child from birth to adulthood.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: History of Psychology
description: A history of the development of various schools and systems of psychological thought.
prerequisites_raw: ( COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4) or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B )

title: Personality Theories
description: A survey of the evolution of personality theory during this century. An overview of major perspectives in the field, with special attention to Freud, Jung, and Adler.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Psychology of Sleep and Consciousness
description: Covers the physiology, neurochemistry, and neuroanatomy associated with sleep, contemporary sleep theory, REM and NREM, phenomenology, sleep disorders, examination of differences between conscious and unconscious cognitive function, the history of sleep and dream theories from ancient time to present day.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Clinical Psychology
description: Provides overview of the clinical psychology field including theories and techniques used in counseling and testing.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Organizational/Industrial Psychology
description: Introduction to applied psychology in organizations, including personnel testing, selection, training and evaluation, job and classification analysis, job satisfaction and motivation, organizational development, leadership, market research, and consumer psychology. Potential ethical problems are discussed.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A or COGS 9B

title: Advanced Industrial-Organizational Psychology
description: Covers advanced topics in industrial-organizational psychology focused on organizational behavior and development; integrates cognitive psychology and business; emphasizes culture, personality, leadership, and motivation in optimizing systems and managing change and conflict.
prerequisites_raw: ( COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4) or COGS 9A or COGS 9B

title: Creativity
description: Introduction to creativity, addressing creativity with respect to cognition, development, neuroscience, education, personality, motivation, and social aspects of creativity.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B )

title: Psychology of Music
description: Introduction to the psychology of music, addressing music with respect to the workings of the ear and brain, the perception and cognition of musical elements like rhythm and melody, and the development of musical skills.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B )

title: Sports Psychology
description: Discusses the field of sports psychology with an emphasis on clinical practice including motivation, goal setting, performance skills, and mental skills. Discusses and utilizes a wide range of techniques designed to enhance performance and manage problems among athletes.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Psychology of Violence
description: Discusses the psychology of violence and aggression with an emphasis on understanding the psychological, social, and physiological roots of violent and aggressive behavior. Psychological treatment techniques and strategies for prevention of aggressive and violent behavior are also discussed.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Moral Psychology
description: Survey course studying moral psychology and philosophy. Empirical research from psychology is supplemented with texts from philosophy for better grounding in philosophical theory.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9B

title: Personality Disorders
description: The history of personality disorder classification; defining characteristics of each disorder; the causes, courses, and outcomes of personality disorders; and information regarding assessment, prevention, and treatments of these disorders.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: PSY 22 or COGS 9C

title: Perception and Sensory Processes
description: A general introduction to the scientific study of sensory processes and perceptual phonomena, with special emphasis in the visual systems.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Neuroscience of Perception
description: Introduces the principles that human perception is determined by the properties of brain circuitry and that these brain circuits evolved to interpret the properties of the physical environment to explore human perception from peripheral sensory organs to cortical processing.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Vision
description: Visual perception and the anatomy and physiology of the visual system. Topics include the retina and the visual pathway; visual sensitivity; color vision; spatial vision; motion perception; and the development of the visual system.

title: Hearing
description: Auditory perception, the anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, and the physics of sound. Topics include neural transduction of sound, sensitivity, sound localization, complex sound perception, and hearing loss.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B

title: Judgment and Decision Making
description: The psychology of human decision making. Theories, models, experiments, and data that inform how people make choices, judgments, and other decisions. Topics include optimality and bias, mental simulation, learning and feedback, expertise, emotional effects, and group decision making.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 9A and COGS 9B

title: Learning and Decision Making
description: The psychological and neural bases of learning about and interacting with the world. Topics include shaping of behavior by rewards and punishments, abstraction of relational information, goal-directed versus habitual decision strategies, social knowledge transmission, and behavioral and substance addictions.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A

title: Human Memory
description: Developments in the area of memory; history of memory research; theories of the nature of memory. Visual memory, recognition memory, high-speed scanning, free recall, short-term memory, mnemonics, retrieval, relationship of memory to thinking. Selected theoretical formulations for memory.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9B

title: Human Problem Solving
description: Modern developments in the psychology of human problem solving. Topics include concept identification, arithmetic, sets, logic puzzles, story problems, group problem solving, and theorem proving.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9B

title: Psychology of Language
description: Examines language using the tools of experimental psychology. From sounds to words to spoken and written sentences, explores how language is used in real time, and how its use reveals how it is represented in the mind.
prerequisites_raw: LSCI 3 and ( LSCI 51 or COGS 56L )

title: African American Psychology
description: Historical overview of the development of black psychology and the African American frame of reference. Topics include personality development, psychological assessment, issues in education, black mental health, and the role of the African American psychologist in the community.

title: Computational Methods for Language Research
description: Focuses on computational methods useful for language research. Students become familiar with software and programming languages used for extracting information from electronic datasets and for creating basic simulations of linguistic cognition. No prior programming experience assumed.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 150 or LSCI 155 or COGS 156A or LSCI 151

title: Introduction to Cognitive Neuroscience
description: Introduction to the neural basis of human perceptual, motor, and cognitive abilities. Topics include sensory perception, motor control, memory, language, attention, emotion, frontal lobe function, functional brain imaging, and neuropsychological disorders.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B )

title: Brain Disorders and Behavior
description: Examines the localization of human brain functions and the effects of neurological disorders on psychological functions such as perception, motor control, language, memory, and decision-making.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B ) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Language and the Brain
description: Research analysis on biological bases of human linguistic capacity. Development, focusing on hemispheric specialization, plasticity; localization of specific linguistic functions in adults, with emphasis on study of aphasias; relation of linguistic capacity to general cognitive capacity, considering research on retardation.
prerequisites_raw: ( COGS 7A or PSCI 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4) or ( COGS 9A or PSCI 11A) and ( COGS 9B or PSCI 11B) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Hearing and the Brain
description: An overview of brain mechanisms of hearing, including perception of simple sounds, speech, and music. Begins with sound itself, and looks at processing by the ear, auditory pathways, auditory cortex, and beyond. Also auditory development, learning, and clinical issues.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 160A or BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

title: Evolution of Language and Music
description: Focuses on the biological evolution of two rather unique human traits: language and music. No other species is capable of “doing” language or music with the complexity that humans can.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B ) or LSCI 3

title: Human Neuropsychology
description: A survey of human brain disorders using a clinical case study approach to illustrate fundamental issues in studying brain and behavior. Topics include sensory deficits, attentional neglect, amnesia, cortical organization, clinical psychopathology, and more.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or COGS 9A

title: Metacognition
description: Critical analysis of primary literature targeting metacognition in perception and memory, including neural correlates. Coverage includes behavioral experimental design, computational models, psychophysics, noninvasive neuroimaging, and neural stimulation approaches.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B )

title: Psychological Anthropology
description: Cultural differences and similarities in personality and behavior. Child-rearing practices and consequent adult personality characteristics, biocultural aspects of child development and attachment, culture and behavior evolutionary models, politically linked personality, cognitive anthropology, psychology of narrative forms, comparative national character studies.
prerequisites_raw: ANTHRO 2A or COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B )

title: Chicano/Latino Families
description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

title: Political Psychology
description: Examination of how psychological theory and research may be used to better understand political thought and behavior. Drawing on theories of learning, cognition, and personality, discusses such topics as the formation of political attitudes, and the process of political decision-making.

title: Deviance
description: Perspectives on deviance and criminality in behavior, institution, community, and myth. The suitability of contemporary theories of deviant behavior.

title: Forensic Psychology: Advanced Seminar
description: Focuses on the psychology of criminal offending, particularly violent behavior. Examines violence, sexual offending, and mental disorder related to crime with regard to clinical assessment and treatment; mental health services within forensic institutions.
prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C) and PSY 102C and ( PSY 161C or CRM/LAW C160 ). Interview required

title: Social Psychology of Networks
description: Review of network methods used in small group and organizational research. Discussion of social psychological literature relevant to the network of study of cognitive social structure, exchange/communication, identity negotiation, and social control. Case study of network datasets exemplifies research issues.

title: Special Topics in Upper-Division Cognitive Sciences
description: Studies in selected areas of cognitive science at the upper-division level. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Directed Group Study
description: Directed study with Cognitive Sciences faculty.

title: Individual Study
description: Independent research with Cognitive Sciences faculty.

title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.

title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.

title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.

title: Proseminar in the Cognitive Sciences
description: Introduction to the conceptual foundations and basic research results in the cognitive sciences for first-year graduate students.

title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences I
description: Logic and set theory are covered during the first three weeks, using an interactive computer system. The remaining seven weeks are devoted to probability theory and cover elementary concepts from samples spaces to Chebychev's Inequality and the moment generating function.

title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences II
description: An introduction to statistical estimation and statistical inference. Topics include sufficiency and the Rao-Blackwell Theorem, completeness and the Lehmann-Scheffe Theorem. The method of maximum likelihood is explored in some detail. Inference in linear models covers regression and analysis of variance.

title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences III
description: Discussion of the fundamentals of statistical inference and computational implementations of common statistical models.

title: Seminar in Professional Development
description: Development of professional skills. Focuses on grant writing and submission process, responsible conduct of research, and ethics training.

title: Seminar in Professional Development
description: Development of professional skills. Focus on scientific presentations and preparation.

title: Seminar in Professional Development
description: Development of professional skills. Focuses on career opportunities, interests and information, and community outreach.

title: Computational Lab Skills for Cognitive Scientists I
description: Provides an in-depth introduction to writing MATLAB programs to run auditory and visual experiments. Topics covered include program structure, stimulus generation, presentation, and data collection.
prerequisites_raw: Knowledge of Python programming

title: Introduction to Statistical Learning
description: Introduction to statistical learning for scientific research. Topics include linear regression, logistic regression, model selection, cross-validation, ridge and Lasso regularization, classification trees, ensemble methods, random forests, unsupervised learning, PCA, k-means clustering, Gaussian mixture models, and PLS regression.
prerequisites_raw: Required: Knowledge of calculus, computer programming, and undergraduate-level statistics

title: Neural Networks and Machine Learning
description: An introduction and review of the current state of the art in neural networks and machine learning with specific emphasis of applications to behavioral and neuroscience data analysis and modeling.

title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences I: Topics in Perception
description: Discusses models of cognition and evidence linking cognition and the brain. Focus is on visual, auditory, and somatic perception and bottom-up mechanisms of attention.

title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences II: Topics in Cognition
description: Discusses models of cognition and evidence linking cognition and the brain. Focus is on emotion, top-down attention, goal-directed behavior, categorization, judgment, and decision-making.

title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences III: Topics in Learning and Development
description: Discusses experimental data, formal models of learning, and evidence linking learning and development to its neural substrates. Topics include Pavlovian and instrumental conditioning, language acquisition, causal reasoning, perceptual learning, category formation, and structure learning.

title: The Mind/Body Problem
description: Multidisciplinary, drawing on information from the fields of quantum physics, computer vision, artificial intelligence, cognition, neurophysiology, philosophy, and psychophysics.

title: Bayesian Cognitive Modeling
description: Considers a range of statistical methods of data analysis and simple cognitive models using the Bayesian graphical modeling framework.

title: Hearing
description: Examines auditory sensation and perception using psychophysical and neuroscientific perspectives. Covers physical aspects of sound; subcortical auditory processing; aspects of sensation and perception such as sensitivity, sound localization, and complex-sound recognition; neuroscientific studies of cortical function; and abnormal auditory processing.

title: Special Topics in Human Cognition
description: Current research in brain/ behavior relationships, human memory, and learning theory is presented.

title: Analysis of Neural Time Series
description: Hands-on introduction to techniques for the analysis of neural time series data, with a primary focus on the electroencephalogram (EEG). Topics may include the physiological basis of EEG, time-frequency analysis, spatial filtering, and methods of assessing connectivity.

title: Advanced Bayesian Cognitive Modeling
description: Considers a range of advanced cognitive process models including models of signal detection, memory retention, category learning, stimulus representation, and reasoning using the Bayesian graphical modeling framework.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 214 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Special Topics in Methodology and Models
description: Current research in cognitive sciences methodologies, concepts, and models is presented.

title: Special Topics in Human Performance
description: Current research in the human issues involved with sensation, perception, and cognition.

title: Cortical Neuroscience
description: Physiology of the cerebral cortex, theoretical neuroscience, and the neural basis of perception.

title: Functional Neuroanatomy
description: It is impossible to truly understand human behavior without some understanding of the physical structure that enables behavior. Examines recent findings in functional neuroantomy through lectures and papers discussing links between particular behaviors and specific brain structures.

title: Introduction to Functional MRI
description: Describes the fundamentals of imaging the human brain function using functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI). Topics include basic fMRI physics, experimental design, and data acquisition and analysis.

title: Computational Neuroscience
description: Introduction to computational neuroscience. Mathematical models of single neurons, neural circuits, thalamocortical systems, and cortical mass action can stimulate single-unit, local field potential, and EEG dynamics. These models are used to investigate mechanisms of sensation, motor control, attention, and consciousness.

title: Cognitive Robotics
description: Introduces concepts for studying cognitive function by embedding brain models on robotic platforms. Topics include robot construction, computer programming, and the notion of embodiment. Students construct simple robots and program these robots to perform different behaviors.

title: Special Topics in Cognitive Neuroscience
description: Current research in cognitive neuroscience.

title: Special Topics in Sensation and Perception
description: Current research in the reception and processing of visual and auditory stimuli presented.

title: Dissertation Research
description: Dissertation research with Cognitive Science faculty.

title: Just Reading: Developing the Reading Experience
description: Develops the reading experience apart from writing. Develops tools for sustained attention in reading practice across a wide range of genres and media from across the globe. Students learn to appreciate elements of reading experience such as attention and perplexity.

title: Topics in Native American and Indigenous Literatures
description: Reading literature by Native American/Indigenous writers from the U.S. and beyond. Texts may include an array of genres including, fiction and non-fiction, poetry and prose, film, and video games.

title: Travels in Comparative Literature
description: Readings in English and in English translation on such topics as love, war, cities, travel writing, politics, fantasy and science fiction, violence.

title: Introduction to Multiculturalism
description: Various themes and forms of literary and cultural production within a multicultural framework, including African American, Asian American, Chicano/Latino, and Native American literatures and cultures.

title: Topics in World Literature
description: Introduction to texts from across the globe and from different historical periods. Readings in English and English translation.

title: World Literature
description: An introduction to the comparative study of literatures and cultures in a global context. Studies literary texts and other media across the borders of various cultures, historical periods, and traditions. All texts are read in English translation.

title: Reading with Theory
description: Introduction to theory and methods of literary and cultural criticism in a global context. Students read theoretical approaches to literature, culture, and ideas. Marx and Freud, e.g., may be studied alongside readings in narrative poetry, film, song lyrics, novel.

title: Cultural Studies
description: Introduces students to a variety of cultural practices (literature, blogs, films, radio, comics) from across the globe. Focuses on the ways that context, genre, and medium (e.g., written, visual, oral) affect how these practices are produced, circulated, and received.

title: Nations, Regions, and Beyond
description: Intensive study of national and regional cultural and literary traditions from across the globe, among them the literary and cultural production of the Middle East, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

title: An Introduction to Translation Studies
description: Focuses on theories of translation and on how these theories help students understand the role of translation in the world. Students develop a critical vocabulary for discussing translation in multiple linguistic traditions and complete a final translation project.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Working knowledge of at least one foreign language

title: Comparative Studies in Literature and Theory
description: In-depth discussion of special topics.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Topics in Comparative Multiculturalism
description: Treats the literatures and cultures of one or more minority groups in California and the United States, including African Americans, Asian Americans, Chicano/Latinos, and Native Americans, and their relations to other national literatures.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Colonialisms and Postcolonialisms
description: Explores topics such as colonialism and race, decolonization, pre- and postcoloniality, globalization, and the cultural dynamics of colonization and subjectivity.

title: Topics in Critical Theory
description: In-depth discussion of one or more theoretical paradigms, debates, or writers (Marxism, Foucault, Queer Theory, Psychoanalysis) with a special focus on what it means to read and think with theoretical texts.

title: Narrative, Pattern, and Text
description: Explores textual patterns, structures, and effects. May include topics such as novel, hypertext, genre, reader responses, intertextuality.

title: Literatures in Dialogue
description: Studies how texts interact across time and space in a global context. Uses concepts of influence, imitation, and parody, to ask, for example, how the Homeric epics can help us understand Caribbean novels and U.S. movies such as Troy.

title: Gender, Sexuality, Race, Class
description: Discusses the roles of differences such as race, class, gender, and sexuality in society, culture, and literature across the globe, covering topics such as theoretical and literary representations of queer sexuality, gender performance, critical race theory.

title: Psychoanalysis and Culture
description: Discusses major psychoanalytic writings of Freud and others in connection with questions of culture.

title: Discourse, Ideologies, and Politics
description: Compares ideologies and systems, e.g., nationalism and fundamentalism, as they affect literature and culture in a global context.

title: Critical Cultural Studies
description: Introduces a variety of ways of understanding cultural phenomena in relation to different power structures. These cultural phenomena may include comics, film, literature, sports, music, festivals, telling stories, or eating out.

title: The Metropolis and Other Cultural Geographies
description: Examines the relationship between space and culture; cultural production in the city, suburb, and/or countryside; spaces in texts and artifacts (film, literature, comics, photographs) in a global context.

title: Literature, Arts, and Media
description: Explores literature and other arts and media in a global context. May include film and electronic media, fine arts, oral cultures, architecture, in an international framework.

title: Literature, History, and Society
description: Explores the relationship between literary texts and their historical and social contexts in an international framework. Courses may address, for example, literary and cultural expressions in social revolutions or the way literary texts talk back to medicine, religion, and anthropology.

title: Literature in Translation
description: The study of literary works in one or more genres in English translation. May be a comparative study of works from several different original languages or a concentration on works from a single cultural/linguistic tradition.

title: World Cinema
description: Comparative analysis of contemporary film in languages other than English.

title: Advanced Seminar in Comparative Literature and Theory
description: Capstone seminar for the Comparative Literature major. Deepens understanding of the field through investigation of a special topic and a substantial research and writing project.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Recommended: COM LIT 60A , COM LIT 60B , and COM LIT 60C

title: Independent Study in Comparative Literature
description: To be taken only when the materials to be studied lie outside the normal run of departmental offerings.

title: History of Comparative Literature and Introduction to Methods and Theories of CL
description: Seminar designed to introduce graduate students in Comparative Literature to the discipline of Comparative Literature. Issues and theories of comparative literary and cultural study are covered. Strongly recommended for first and second year students before the M.A. exam and review.

title: Topics in Theories of Translation
description: The reproduction, translation, and transfer of literary and cultural, ideological and political, and symbolic codes and texts have long been the object of study in Comparative Literature. Addresses the diverse ways in which expressive systems interact and intersect.

title: Comparative Studies
description: Studies in selected areas of Comparative Literature. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Professionalization Seminar
description: The first of two required professionalization seminars in Comparative Literature. Intended for first and second year students and covers preparation for the M.A. and Ph.D. exams, conference presentations, teaching and classroom management, and publishing journals.

title: Professionalization Seminar
description: The second of two required professionalization seminars in Comparative Literature. Intended for fourth and fifth year students and covers course design, applying for grants, dissertation prospectus and support, and the job application process.
prerequisites_raw: COM LIT 280A with a minimum grade of B

title: Reading and Conference
description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Guided Reading Course
description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Teaching Practicum
description: Graduate students develop their pedagogical practices by accompanying a professor teaching a UCI undergraduate class. Meets individually with the professor to discuss relevant pedagogical practices, syllabus design, lecturing, assessment, classroom management, etc. Actively participates in one teaching component.

title: Pre-Dissertation Research
description: Taken under the direction of the graduate advisor or committee member in preparation for the Ph.D. exam. It can be taken after students have completed the M.A. review and program coursework requirements.
